newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gold Peak cleared to dilute S'pore stakes.
newsitem.headline: Gold Peak cleared to dilute S'pore stakes.

text.p: Gold Peak Industries (Holdings) Ltd said on Thursday it had been cleared to decide whether to cut its stakes in GP Batteries International Ltd and Clipsal Industries Holdings Ltd.

It said shareholders had voted at an extraordinary general meeting to authorise directors to decide "at their sole discretion" on whether to cut Gold Peak's stakes in the two Singapore-listed companies.

"The mandate granted by our shareholders will give GP Batteries and Clipsal Industries maximum flexibility in fundraising," Victor Lo, chairman and chief executive of Gold Peak Industries said in a statement.
Gold Peak owned 50.13 percent of GP Batteries and 50.10 percent of Clipsal Industries as at March 24, 1997, it said.
It said shareholders mandated Gold Peak to allow its shareholding to be diluted if the two units issued new shares:
- under their general mandates, a maximum of 10 percent;
- upon exercise of outstanding warrants by holders other than Gold Peak;
- or under existing share options schemes.
If the stakes in the units fell to 50 percent or less, they would no longer be consolidated in Gold Peak's accounts, significantly cutting Gold Peak's gearing ratio, it said.
This would also allow it additional capacity in financing potential new investments, Gold Peak said.
Lo said Gold Peak did not anticipate any material change in the management or operation of the two companies even if they were de-consolidated in the future.
Gold Peak shares closed down HK$0.10 at HK$5.05.
